chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Harun who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Singing leads to hypocrisy and results in poverty.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and material consequences of singing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking al-aghani (singing) to both spiritual hypocrisy (nifaq) and material poverty, reflecting the Shia tradition of viewing sensory indulgence as a gateway to moral decay. This hadith is often interpreted by scholars as indicating that the distraction of the heart from divine remembrance through entertainment erodes sincerity and, by extension, one's capacity for worldly sustenance.
